note: Ground truth for the drifted fixture. `seeded` are real defects a review should find; `traps` are things that LOOK like defects and must not be reported. Recall is measured against seeded, false-positive rate against traps.
matching: Each seeded defect lists its `sides`. A side is a list of interchangeable distinctive phrases, any one of which identifies that side. A defect counts as found when a single finding's quotes hit at least two different sides (or the only side, for a one-sided defect). Phrases are deliberately SHORT and central: a reviewer legitimately chooses how much of a sentence to quote, and ground truth must not penalise a correct finding for quoting a different span. Every phrase must still appear verbatim in the fixture, which tests/fixture.test.ts enforces.

seeded.summary: Deploy timing advice conflicts with no shared vocabulary: 'Shipping on a Friday afternoon is fine' versus 'Never deploy at the end of the week'. Only the claim-ledger reduce pass can join these.
sides: Shipping on a Friday afternoon is fine
Never deploy at the end of the week.
seeded.history: The first version of this defect read 'Deploy during business hours' against 'Never deploy at the end of the week'. Three independent refuters killed it, correctly: those two rules are jointly satisfiable by deploying Monday to Thursday, so it was an incompleteness rather than a contradiction. Rewritten to be unambiguous, because this defect exists to measure whether the claim ledger can join two statements with NO shared vocabulary -- not to measure whether refuters can spot a weak claim, which they demonstrably can.
seeded.isolationLimit: This fixture is ~130 lines, which is a single shard, so the shard reader sees both documents and can reach this defect without the claim ledger -- and on the second run it did. The no-shared-vocabulary property still holds and is gate-tested, but the reduce pass is not ISOLATED here. Proving the ledger is load-bearing needs a fixture large enough to shard, so the two halves land in different readers. Until then, the evidence for the mechanism is the first run, where the shard reader had both documents in front of it and still missed the conflict that the ledger caught.
